title: UBS Boosts Profitability Ambitions as Cost Savings Exceed Expectations
detail:
UBS Boosts Profitability Ambitions as Cost Savings Exceed Expectations
Zacks Equity Research
Mon, November 2, 2026 at 8:58 AM MST 4 min read
UBS
UBS
C
DB
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

UBS Group AG UBS is making strong progress toward its 2026 profitability and efficiency targets. During the third quarter of 2026, UBS reported an underlying return on common equity tier 1 (ROCET1) of 16.7% and an underlying cost/income ratio of 68.7%. In light of these results, management expects to exceed its exit-rate ROCET1 target of approximately 15% and maintain the cost/income ratio below 70% for full-year 2026, as outlined in its 2025 annual report.

Strong revenue growth across UBS's core businesses is supporting its improving profitability. In the third quarter of 2026, underlying revenues increased 10% year over year to $13.4 billion, while underlying profit before tax rose 14% to $4.1 billion. Growth in Global Wealth Management and Investment Banking, driven by client activity and market-related revenues, supported this performance. Global Markets also posted solid revenue growth, while Global Wealth Management continued to attract strong net new assets, supporting UBS's higher-return ambitions.

UBS' Revenue Trend in Q3
UBS Group AG

Image Source: UBS Group AG

Alongside this revenue growth, continued cost discipline is supporting UBS's efforts to improve operating efficiency. As of Sept. 30, 2026, the company's cumulative gross cost savings reached $13.2 billion. Management expects the metric to reach nearly $13.7 billion by year-end 2026, exceeding its previous ambition of $13.5 billion. Ongoing restructuring, simplification and tighter cost controls are helping reduce the expense base and further improve the cost/income ratio.

Progress in the Credit Suisse integration (acquired in June 2023) is further supporting the bank's cost-reduction efforts. UBS remains on track to substantially complete the integration by the end of 2026. As of Sept. 30, 2026, approximately 90% of the legacy Credit Suisse IT applications slated for decommissioning had been fully decommissioned, while nearly all the remaining applications were no longer in use. Removing duplicate systems and infrastructure is helping simplify operations, reduce complexity and capture further cost efficiencies from the acquisition.

Overall, strong revenue growth, continued cost discipline and progress in the Credit Suisse integration are supporting UBS's efforts to achieve its 2026 targets. These factors also provide a foundation for the bank's longer-term ambitions of delivering reported ROCET1 of nearly 18% and a reported cost/income ratio of around 67% by 2028. Yet, evolving Swiss capital regulations and the ability to sustain revenue growth while controlling expenses remain key factors to watch.

JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM), Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), and Citigroup (NYSE: C) are putting billions behind their share buyback programs, with each bank authorizing at least $30 billion in repurchases.

All three banks released third-quarter results in mid-October, offering updates on their finances and their future plans. Which ones have actually followed through on these share repurchase agreements, shrinking their share count and giving investors more bang for their investment buck?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
JPMorgan has the biggest buyback but the slowest pace

In June 2026, JPMorgan's board authorized a new $50 billion common stock repurchase program, effective July 1. And during the third quarter, JPMorgan repurchased around $1 billion in common stock but recorded only $664 million in net repurchases. In other words, that gross amount used only about 2% of the new authorization.

And not surprisingly, the impact on the share count was modest. The company ended September with 2.656 billion common shares outstanding, compared with 2.722 billion a year earlier. That means its share count declined just 2.4% year over year.

There's a reason for the slower pace.

Management has emphasized that repurchases must compete with other uses of capital, including investments in the business, lending opportunities, and the maintenance of a strong balance sheet. The bank also faces risks around weaker credit quality and investment banking activity.

On top of that, at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 13 times, its valuation also leaves less room for disappointment than its peers'.

A faster $40 billion buyback is shrinking Bank of America's share count

Bank of America has had a $40 billion common stock repurchase authorization in place since Aug. 1, 2025. By June 30, 2026, the bank had around $17 billion remaining under the authorization after repurchasing $13.2 billion in the first half of the year. Then, during the third quarter, it repurchased another $6 billion of common stock.

That brings the program's total repurchases to $29 billion, leaving $11 billion available. Put differently, it has used roughly 73% of the authorization in about 14 months and at its current pace, that remaining amount could be used relatively quickly.

Investing.com -- Citi initiated coverage of French retail technology company Vusiongroup SA (EPA:VU) with a "buy" rating, arguing that the market is underestimating its growth potential beyond a major Walmart rollout and the expansion of electronic shelf labels across global retailers.

The bank set a price target of €250, implying around 84% upside from the October 30 closing price of €135.80, and assigned the stock a "high risk" designation due to its historical volatility.

In a research note published Monday, Citi said Vusion was the global leader in electronic shelf labels (ESLs), with an estimated 40% share of a market that reached about €2.3 billion in 2025. Despite strong industry growth, global ESL penetration remains around 20%, leaving considerable room for further adoption as retailers seek to reduce labour costs and improve operational efficiency.

Citi believes Vusion can defend its market position as adoption increases, with additional growth coming from replacement cycles, software subscriptions and retail media.

The bank also sees scope for margin expansion as higher-margin value-added services become a larger share of revenue. Vusion's October acquisition of Spanish retail media company In-Store Media is expected to support that shift, with Citi estimating that a richer services mix could add 480 basis points to variable cost margins through 2028.

Citi argued that investors are overly concerned about a potential decline in sales following completion of Vusion's major U.S. Walmart electronic shelf label rollout. Recent contracts with retailers including Carrefour, Morrisons, Walmart Mexico and Walmart Canada should help support future demand, it said.

The bank opened a positive catalyst watch ahead of Vusion's November 18 capital markets day, which it views as a potential trigger for a valuation re-rating.

Key risks include weaker-than-expected demand after the Walmart rollout, increased competition, cybersecurity threats and possible regulatory restrictions on electronic pricing labels.

Citigroup reported that credit card delinquency ratios in the third quarter were better than feared, indicating that consumer credit quality in its card portfolio remained manageable even as households dealt with inflation pressures.

This resilience in Citigroup's card book points to disciplined underwriting and collections, which can influence how investors think about future loss provisioning and the durability of its consumer earnings stream.

We will now look at how Citigroup's improving card delinquency profile could influence the broader investment narrative investors are using.

Scan how other large banks with card exposure and bond issuance profiles similar to Citigroup are positioning for the next phase of credit risk using the curated 29 resilient stocks with low risk scores.

Citigroup Investment Narrative Recap

To own Citigroup, you need to believe the bank can keep turning its global services, cards and wealth engines into steady earnings, while keeping risk and costs under control. The recent run of medium and long dated fixed income offerings does not materially change that near term equation. In the short term, the key swing factor remains credit quality and loan loss provisioning in U.S. cards.

The biggest risk still sits in operational and regulatory execution rather than in this funding activity. Any lapse in controls or an unexpected deterioration in credit could pressure margins and slow the effort to sustain double digit returns on tangible common equity.

The recent cluster of Citigroup fixed income deals, including new senior unsecured and subordinated notes across 2028 to 2046 maturities, is the most relevant development right now. These issues add term funding and help shape the liability profile alongside the announced redemptions of notes due in 2026, which together refresh the debt stack.

For you as a shareholder, the interest is indirect. Smooth access to bond markets supports Citigroup's ability to fund its growing services and cards books while still running a capital return program and preparing for moves like the Banamex IPO. The execution risk is that higher funding costs or regulatory shifts eat into the margin improvements investors are watching.

Citigroup's analyst narrative points to forecast revenue of US$108.8b and projected earnings of US$22.4b by 2029. This is based on an assumed 9.3% yearly revenue growth rate and an earnings increase of about US$4.5b from current earnings of US$17.9b.
